sections.title: I. Macroeconomic Developments
sections.description: GDP growth, inflation, exchange rate, monetary policy, fiscal position, key industry performance

events.title: USD Falls to 7-Year Low at PYG 6,000; Guaraní Ranks 3rd Best-Performing Currency in Latin America (2026-07-31)
events.summary: The US dollar closed at PYG 6,000 for sale and PYG 5,920 for purchase at end-July 2026, its lowest level in seven years (since 2019). The guaraní has appreciated 8.13% YTD and the dollar depreciated ~20% year-on-year. Bloomberg ranked the guaraní as Latin America's 3rd best-performing currency in 2026 behind Colombian peso (+14.60%) and Costa Rican colón (+10.17%). Exporters expressed alarm over shrinking margins, while importers and consumers benefit from lower costs. The BCP estimates a mild recovery to PYG 6,300 by year-end due to import seasonality.

events.title: BCP Holds Policy Rate at 5.50% for Third Consecutive Month; No FX Intervention in H1 2026 (2026-07-30)
events.summary: The Central Bank of Paraguay maintained its monetary policy rate at 5.50% for the third consecutive month. The BCP has not conducted any foreign exchange interventions in H1 2026, respecting the flexible exchange rate regime. The real ex-ante policy rate remains within the BCP's neutral range (1.3%–2.6%). Annual inflation eased to 2.7% in January 2026, well below the new 3.5% target. The BCP offered exporters forward contracts as hedging tools amid the strong guaraní.

events.title: June Trade Surplus Hits USD 47.09 Million; Exports Surge 25.1% YoY Driven by Record Soybean Shipments (2026-07-30)
events.summary: Paraguay registered a trade surplus of USD 47.09 million in June 2026, with exports reaching USD 1.740 billion (+25.1% year-on-year), driven by record soybean shipments, soybean oil, and agricultural products. The strong export performance — combined with investment-grade ratings and robust FDI — continues to supply abundant foreign currency, reinforcing the guaraní's appreciation trend. The bumper soybean harvest underpins the inflows.

events.title: Fitch Begins Annual Credit Rating Review; Moody's Reaffirms Baa3 Investment Grade for Third Year (2026-07-31)
events.summary: Fitch Ratings initiated its annual review of Paraguay's sovereign credit rating on July 31, meeting with President Santiago Peña to assess macroeconomic indicators. Paraguay currently holds BB+ with positive outlook from Fitch — one notch below investment grade. This follows Moody's July 18 reaffirmation of Baa3 (investment grade, stable outlook), marking three consecutive years at investment grade, and S&P's upgrade to BBB- in December 2025. Q1 2026 GDP growth reached 5.8% YoY. Full-year 2026 growth is projected at 4.2%.

sections.title: II. Political & Policy Developments
sections.description: Major legislation, policy adjustments, foreign investment regulation, tax reform, investment incentives

events.title: President Peña Replaces ANDE Chief; Orders 'Strictly Technical' Tariff Policy to Unblock Data Center Investments (2026-07-30)
events.summary: President Santiago Peña replaced ANDE president Félix Sosa with Miguel Báez Reyes on July 28, ordering an end to internal pressures and a transition to 'strictly technical and transparent' electricity tariffs to guarantee financial sustainability and give certainty to private investors. Báez warned that Paraguay's energy surplus could be exhausted between 2030–2031, making it urgent to explore new generation sources (solar, gas, etc.). The government simultaneously accelerated the AI data center law, previously blocked by Sosa's resistance. Total power demand from interested industries reaches 5,000 MW.

events.title: Government Accelerates AI Data Center Law After ANDE Leadership Change; X8Cloud, HIVE, Dominion Interested (2026-07-28)
events.summary: With new ANDE leadership, the government fast-tracked the AI data center bill within the Presidential Business Advisory Council. Companies including X8Cloud Inc. (USA), HIVE Digital, and Dominion (Canada) are interested in investing. The new ANDE administration committed to evaluating all proposals with technical, financial, and technological criteria. The former ANDE chief had blocked progress due to disputes related to the Atome hydrogen project (Decreto 5307 was derogated).

events.title: Paraguay and Ecuador Sign Five Bilateral Agreements; Ecuadorian Firms Announce USD 200M+ Investment Plans (2026-07-31)
events.summary: President Peña visited Quito on July 29, meeting President Daniel Noboa and signing five agreements covering: economic complementarity study (with ALADI support), air services, security and defense cooperation (including extradition treaty), and women's empowerment. During the visit, Ecuadorian firms Novacero and Swissôtel announced plans to invest over USD 200 million in Paraguay in hospitality, commerce, and steel, citing the country's stability, Triple-10 tax regime, and investment incentives.

events.title: Peña and Báez Back Natural Resource Exploration in Médanos del Chaco National Park (2026-07-30)
events.summary: President Peña and new ANDE chief Báez expressed support for exploring gas and mineral resources within the Médanos del Chaco National Park, arguing urgency in finding alternative energy sources. Vice Minister of Mines and Energy Mauricio Bejarano backed the stance, though the Environment Ministry (MADES) had previously issued an adverse opinion. MOPC and the Association of Geologists also advanced a new Mining Code to modernize regulations and attract foreign investment.

events.title: MEF Issues USD 59.8 Million in Local Market Bonds; Fiscal Deficit Converging to 1.5% of GDP (2026-07-29)
events.summary: Paraguay's Ministry of Economy and Finance issued bonds worth USD 59.8 million in the local market, continuing diversification of financing sources. The 2026 fiscal deficit is projected to narrow to 1.5% of GDP under the Fiscal Responsibility Law, with public debt at approximately 38% of GDP — significantly below the median for Baa3-rated sovereigns. Paraguay's fiscal pressure ratio stands at just 14% of GDP, second-lowest in the region after Panama.

sections.title: III. Social & Security Situation
sections.description: Labor market, social stability, public security, employment data

events.title: Minimum Wage Reajusted 5% to PYG 3,044,000 Effective July 1; MTESS Demands Compliance (2026-07-30)
events.summary: The Executive Branch implemented a 5% minimum wage increase effective July 1, 2026, via Decree No. 6225/2026, raising the monthly minimum to PYG 3,044,000 (daily PYG 117,077). The MTESS urged private-sector workers to report non-compliance, which carries fines of up to 30 daily minimum wages per affected worker plus back-pay obligations. The adjustment follows CONASAM's recommendation based on CPI variation. Employer IPS contributions remain at 16.5% of gross salary.

events.title: EPP Guerrilla Attack Kills 3 Officers at Canindeyú Police Station; Organized Crime Nexus Exposed (2026-07-23)
events.summary: Between 20–30 armed men attacked a police station in Colonia Naranjito, Canindeyú department on July 23, killing two police officers and one civilian employee, and wounding two other officers. Authorities attribute the assault to the Marxist guerrilla group EPP (Ejército del Pueblo Paraguayo), but later acknowledged a possible EPP-narcotrafficking alliance with PCC and Comando Vermelho. The attack exposed serious intelligence failures. Canindeyú is the second-highest department for cocaine, marijuana, and arms trafficking after Amambay, serving as a drug transit route to Brazil.

events.title: Organized Crime and Agribusiness Pressure Indigenous Communities; Police Checkpoints Called 'Crime Tolls' (2026-07-30)
events.summary: The peasant community '1° de Marzo Joaju' (Ybyrarobana, Canindeyú) denounced that organized crime and agribusiness interests are using insecurity as a pretext to pressure the state for their eviction from 4,500 hectares of public land. Criminologist Juan Martens criticized institutional weakness and 'official propaganda' portraying Paraguay as safe. Police checkpoints on Route PY03 have reportedly become 'organized crime tolls.' The government suggested the existence of 'radicalized peasants,' a version the communities deny.

events.title: 16 Femicides Recorded in First 7 Months of 2026; Citizens Mobilize in Curuguaty for Justice (2026-07-30)
events.summary: Paraguay registered 16 femicide victims and 24 attempted femicide cases between January and July 2026, with three deaths occurring in the 72 hours before July 30. Citizens organized a mobilization in Curuguaty on July 30 to demand justice and the capture of a suspect. The events reflect persistent gender-based violence and growing public demand for institutional response.

sections.title: IV. International Relations & Diplomacy
sections.description: Paraguay's relations with major countries, Mercosur dynamics, China-Taiwan relations

events.title: Paraguay Offers Conditional Trade Opening to China Without Breaking Taiwan Ties; Beijing Categorically Rejects (2026-07-01)
events.summary: At the Mercosur Summit in Luque, Foreign Minister Rubén Ramírez stated Paraguay is open to trade with China provided no conditions are imposed regarding its diplomatic ties with Taiwan. China's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun rejected the proposal, calling on Paraguay 'to stand on the right side of history' and not remain in 'self-isolation.' Chinese expert Sun Hongbo described the dual-channel approach as 'wishful thinking.' Paraguay remains Taiwan's sole diplomatic ally in South America and the only Mercosur member without ties to Beijing. China is Paraguay's largest supplier of goods, including mobile phones and data processing equipment.

events.title: Paraguay Demands Equitable EU Export Quotas at Mercosur Summit; 'First-Come, First-Served' System Favors Brazil (2026-07-01)
events.summary: At the 68th Mercosur Summit in Asunción, President Peña expressed 'bitter disappointment' with the EU-Mercosur trade deal's implementation, demanding equitable distribution of export quotas for beef and rice. The 2026 zero-tariff beef quota is 6,000 tons, but without an internal distribution agreement, a 'first-come, first-served' system favors larger economies, particularly Brazil. Paraguay, as a landlocked country with higher logistics costs, argues the system reproduces asymmetries. The bloc's rotating presidency passed to Uruguay.

events.title: US-Paraguay Trade Tops USD 1.5 Billion; AmCham Targets USD 2 Billion with 'Plan Paraguay 2x' (2026-07-30)
events.summary: Bilateral trade between Paraguay and the US surpassed USD 1.5 billion, with Paraguayan exports exceeding USD 500 million in 2025. AmCham Paraguay president Elías Saba met with Industry Minister Marco Riquelme on July 30. 'Plan Paraguay 2x' targets an additional USD 670 million in exports over the next decade, aiming to surpass USD 1 billion by 2035. Key sectors: AI/data centers, logistics/nearshoring, food, and infrastructure. In April 2026, Paraguayan exports to the US grew 31.9% YoY. Paraguay was excluded from new US tariffs imposed on ~60 trading partners.

events.title: Paraguay-Taiwan Announce Joint 'World's Largest AI Hub' for South America (2026-05-11)
events.summary: During President Peña's visit to Taiwan in May 2026, Paraguay and Taiwan announced a partnership to create 'the world's largest AI hub,' jointly funded by both governments, combining Taiwanese technology with Paraguay's clean energy surplus. Paraguay also formally joined LACTO (Latin American and Caribbean Trade Office) in Taipei on July 25 to strengthen commercial exchange. The alliance reinforces Paraguay's strategic pivot toward becoming a regional digital infrastructure hub while deepening its Taiwan diplomatic alignment.

sections.title: V. Industry Spotlight: Telecom, Digital Energy & AI
sections.description: 5G spectrum & commercial progress, fiber infrastructure, digital energy investment, AI data center development, sector policy

events.title: Tigo and Personal Submit Bids for Second 5G Spectrum Auction; USD 40M Minimum Investment Each (2026-07-10)
events.summary: Tigo (Telefónica Celular del Paraguay) and Personal (Núcleo S.A.) submitted bids on July 10 for CONATEL's second 5G spectrum tender (No. 01/2026), covering 2.3 GHz and 3.5 GHz bands. Each must commit a minimum USD 40 million in secure network infrastructure with 5G NR Release 15+ compatible equipment. Both operators had declined the first 2025 auction due to Chinese vendor restrictions (Huawei/ZTE excluded). Tigo leads the market with 3.16M mobile internet users, followed by Personal (1.66M) and Claro (947K).

events.title: HIVE Digital Expands to 400 MW in Paraguay; Launches BUZZ Cloud AI Platform in Asunción (2026-Q3)
events.summary: HIVE Digital Technologies is expanding its Yguazú facility by +100 MW (Phase 3), reaching 400 MW total in Paraguay. Construction began in early 2026 with commissioning expected Q3 2026. HIVE targets 35 EH/s in Bitcoin mining and 5x growth in HPC/AI capacity for 2026. The BUZZ Cloud AI platform launched at a Tier III data center in Asunción in Q1 2026, offering GPU clusters for AI training and inference. HIVE's total global capacity reaches 540 MW, with Paraguay as its largest operation.

events.title: IDB Invest and Proparco Invest USD 100M in Millicom/Tigo for 4G/5G and Fiber Expansion Across 7 Countries Including Paraguay (2026-03-30)
events.summary: IDB Invest and Proparco invested USD 100 million in Millicom (Tigo) bonds to fund 4G/4.5G/5G network modernization and fiber optic expansion across seven Latin American countries, including Paraguay. Data traffic is projected to triple by 2030. Additionally, Tigo Paraguay issued ~USD 77 million in local-currency bonds in January 2026 — a historic guaraní-denominated operation strengthening its domestic investment capacity.

events.title: Nubicom's USD 200M 5G Pledge Under Comptroller Investigation; Zero Deployment Progress to Date (2026-07-15)
events.summary: Nubicom, the Argentine operator that won 200 MHz of 3.5 GHz spectrum in Paraguay's first 5G auction with a USD 200 million investment pledge, faces a Comptroller General investigation for failing to deploy any infrastructure. Required to establish a local subsidiary within six weeks and begin deployment within six months, Nubicom met neither deadline. The controversy has raised questions about the first auction's integrity and the operator's ties to business associates of President Peña. Claro, by contrast, launched Paraguay's first commercial 5G network in December 2025.

events.title: 1,600 Starlink Kits Deployed for Schools; 95 Chaco Schools Connected; 18,000 km National Fiber Network Operational (2026-07-30)
events.summary: MITIC, COPACO, MEC, CONATEL, and Starlink are deploying 1,600 Starlink kits in remote educational institutions under 'Connecting Opportunities for Paraguay's Future.' The first 95 Chaco schools are already connected. The government enabled 100+ free internet points serving 1.3 million citizens, adding to 400+ public Wi-Fi points. The National Fiber Optic Network (RNFO) spans 18,000 km, though FTTH penetration remains at ~15%. Fixed broadband revenue is projected to grow from USD 219.3M (2024) to USD 289.1M (2029), CAGR 5.7%.

sections.title: VI. Key Client Movements
sections.description: Tracking strategic deployments, investment plans, network construction, and technology choices of Paraguay's key telecom clients

events.title: Claro (América Móvil) — Paraguay's First 5G Network Operational; USD 35M Investment with Nokia; 200 Base Stations Committed (2026-07-30)
events.summary: Claro launched Paraguay's first commercial 5G network in December 2025 with USD 35 million initial investment, deploying Nokia Massive MIMO radios with IPAA+ technology. Service covers Greater Asunción, Ciudad del Este, Encarnación, Coronel Oviedo, and Pedro Juan Caballero. Claro acquired 200 MHz in the 3.5 GHz band for USD 2.021 million. GM Alfredo Alcaraz confirmed sustained expansion through 2026. Claro must deploy at least 200 base stations, with 10% serving state entities. Holds 947,000 mobile internet users.

events.title: Tigo (Millicom) — USD 177M Combined Funding for 5G Bid, Fiber Expansion and Network Modernization (2026-07-30)
events.summary: Tigo Paraguay secured combined funding of ~USD 177 million: USD 100 million from IDB Invest/Proparco for regional 4G/5G/fiber expansion (March 2026) and ~USD 77 million in local-currency bond issuance (January 2026). Tigo submitted its bid for the second 5G spectrum auction on July 10, committing at least USD 40 million. As market leader with 3.16M mobile internet users (55% share) and ~3,100 employees, Tigo is best positioned for 5G/fiber expansion. The company has operated in Paraguay since 1992.

events.title: Personal (Núcleo S.A. / Telecom Argentina) — Enters Second 5G Auction After Boycotting First; USD 40M Minimum Commitment (2026-07-10)
events.summary: Personal (Núcleo S.A., subsidiary of Telecom Argentina) submitted its bid for CONATEL's second 5G spectrum auction on July 10, committing a minimum USD 40 million. Personal had declined the first 2025 auction due to Chinese vendor restrictions. As Paraguay's second-largest operator with 1.66M mobile internet users, Personal is strong in urban fiber deployment and is rated the most recommended for speed. Its renewed commitment signals confidence in Paraguay's 5G market framework.

events.title: Nubicom — USD 200M 5G Investment Under Investigation; Zero Deployment; Credibility Crisis (2026-07-15)
events.summary: Nubicom, the Argentine operator that won 200 MHz in Paraguay's first 5G auction (August 2025) with a USD 200 million pledge, faces a Comptroller General investigation for zero deployment progress. The company had no prior mobile infrastructure in either Argentina or Paraguay. The investigation contrasts sharply with Claro's successful 5G launch and the entry of Tigo and Personal in the second auction. Questions persist about Nubicom's technical capacity and the integrity of the original auction process.

sections.title: VII. Comprehensive Impact Analysis for Enterprises
sections.description: Integrating macro environment, industry trends, and client movements to assess enterprise impact across cost, market, and compliance dimensions
sections.impact_analysis:
=== VII. Comprehensive Impact Analysis for Enterprises ===

**1. Macroeconomic: Strong Fundamentals with Currency Tension Rising**

The BCP's hold at 5.50% with inflation below the 3.5% target confirms Paraguay's macroeconomic stability. GDP grew 6.6% in 2025 with Q1 2026 at 5.8% YoY. For enterprises, this means stable financing costs and no near-term tightening risk. However, the guaraní's 8.13% YTD appreciation (dollar at 7-year low of PYG 6,000) creates a clear winners/losers split: importers of equipment and technology inputs benefit; agro-exporters face margin compression. The BCP's refusal to intervene and the Fed's rate hold suggest the strong guaraní may persist. Businesses with peso revenues and dollar costs should actively use BCP forward contracts.

🟡 Risk: Sustained appreciation could trigger policy response (BCP intervention or rate cuts). Monitor BCP's August EVE survey.


**2. Energy & Regulatory: Inflection Point for Digital Infrastructure**

The July 28 ANDE leadership change is the single most consequential policy event of the period. By removing Félix Sosa, who had blocked the AI data center law, President Peña unblocked the key bottleneck for energy-intensive digital investment. With ~5 GW surplus hydroelectric capacity, 100% renewable at ~USD 41/MWh (vs. USD 113/MWh in Brazil), and a pending data center law, Paraguay's value proposition is exceptionally strong. The Báez appointment and his commitment to 'strictly technical tariffs' provide near-term regulatory clarity, though the energy surplus warning (exhaustion by 2030-2031) signals the window for securing favorable long-term energy contracts may be closing.

🟢 Opportunity: Window for large-scale energy contracts. 🟡 Risk: Energy surplus finite; early movers will lock in best terms.


**3. Security & Operational Risk: Canindeyú Demands Immediate Attention**

The July 23 Naranjito police station attack is the most serious guerrilla incident in months. The EPP-narcotrafficking convergence (PCC, Comando Vermelho) in the Brazil border zone transforms Canindeyú from chronic concern to acute operational risk. Companies with rural telecom sites, field teams, or logistics operations in Canindeyú, Alto Paraná, or Amambay should immediately review security protocols. The contradictory government narratives about attack authorship undermine confidence in security coordination.

🔴 Risk: Canindeyú — immediate security concern. 🟡 Risk: Broader northern border zone requires monitoring.


**4. Telecom & Digital Infrastructure: 5G Competition Entering New Phase**

CONATEL's second 5G auction with Tigo and Personal transforms Paraguay's 5G landscape from Claro-only to three-operator competition. The combined minimum investment of USD 80M+ from the two incumbents, plus their existing funding (Tigo USD 177M), signals a credible buildout cycle. Equipment procurement opportunities expand for non-Chinese vendors (Nokia, Ericsson). The Nubicom investigation reinforces the need for rigorous counterparty due diligence.

🟢 Opportunity: Competitive 5G pricing, expanded coverage, procurement demand for network equipment and services.


**5. Diplomatic & Trade: Broadening Partnerships, Persistent Taiwan Constraint**

Paraguay's diplomatic activity (US trade momentum, Ecuador agreements, India agricultural cooperation) shows deliberate diversification. The US tariff exemption while ~60 other nations face duties is a concrete competitive advantage. However, Beijing's categorical rejection of Paraguay's conditional trade proposal (July 1) confirms the Taiwan strait remains the binding diplomatic constraint for Chinese enterprises in regulated sectors.

sections.title: VIII. China-Specific Strategic Impact & Recommendations
sections.description: Targeted analysis of special risks and opportunities for Chinese enterprises, including policy risk, diplomatic risk, and business recommendations
sections.impact_analysis:
=== VIII. China-Specific Strategic Impact & Recommendations ===

**1. Diplomatic Framework: No Structural Change, Commercial Signals Intensify**

Paraguay remains the only South American nation recognizing Taiwan and the only Mercosur member without China ties. Beijing's categorical rejection (July 1) of Paraguay's 'trade without diplomatic conditions' proposal confirms no near-term breakthrough. The Paraguay-Taiwan 'world's largest AI hub' joint announcement (May 2026) and LACTO trade office incorporation (July 25) further entrench the Taiwan alignment. For Chinese enterprises, the binding constraint remains: exclusion from 5G equipment (Huawei/ZTE banned under 'trusted vendor' clauses), restricted government procurement, and no bilateral investment treaty.


**2. Sector-Specific Assessment:**

🔴 **5G Equipment Market — Closed.** CONATEL's 'trusted vendor' framework continues to exclude Chinese RAN vendors. Both Claro (Nokia) and the Tigo/Personal second auction follow Western vendor paths. No re-entry pathway without diplomatic shift.

🟢 **Data Center Equipment & Infrastructure — High Potential, Low Politicization.** HIVE's 400 MW, X8Cloud's multibillion-dollar proposal, and the pending AI data center law create demand for: power distribution, cooling systems, server racks, fiber connectivity, and modular data center solutions. These categories face fewer political barriers than core telecom. Chinese manufacturers can supply through OEM/white-label channels or regional subsidiaries.

🟢 **Renewable Energy Equipment — Growing Market.** The ANDE leadership change unblocks solar, battery storage, and grid equipment procurement as Paraguay diversifies beyond hydro. Chinese cost competitiveness in solar panels, inverters, and BESS is strong. The Maquila regime (1% tax on value-added) enables local assembly for the Mercosur-EU market.

🟡 **Mining Equipment & Critical Minerals Supply Chain — Long-term Play.** The new Mining Code, Médanos del Chaco exploration, and US Critical Minerals MoU create medium-term opportunities. Chinese mining equipment and processing technology could participate, though the US MoU introduces geopolitical competition.

🟢 **Agritech — Underpenetrated Market.** Paraguay's agricultural economy (soybeans, beef, grains) has nascent technology adoption. Chinese agritech (drones, precision agriculture, irrigation) can enter through commercial B2B channels without diplomatic barriers.


**3. Strategic Recommendations:**

1. **Structure through third-country vehicles** (Singapore, Netherlands, UAE) to mitigate diplomatic risk and benefit from Paraguay's investment protection framework.
2. **Prioritize the Brazil-Paraguay corridor.** Brazil's large Chinese business community (São Paulo, Foz do Iguaçu) provides proximity-based support networks. The 62% surge in foreign residency applications (64% Brazilian) validates this pathway.
3. **Engage multilateral development banks (IDB, CAF)** for de-risked infrastructure project entry. IDB's USD 130M digital infrastructure financing and CAF's energy reform involvement provide entry points.
4. **Leverage the Maquila regime (1% tax) and Investor Pass** for manufacturing/assembly targeting Mercosur-EU markets under the newly implemented trade agreement.
5. **Monitor energy reform timeline closely.** The UIP-MIC-CAF proposals for independent regulator and private generation opening, if implemented, would create significant equipment opportunities.
6. **Prepare for binary diplomatic risk.** Any Taiwan-China shift would fundamentally alter the competitive landscape. Maintain scenario plans for both continuity and change.


**4. Priority Sector Matrix:**

| Sector | Opportunity | Timeframe | Entry Strategy |
|--------|------------|-----------|----------------|
| Data center equipment & infrastructure | 🟢 High | 2026-2027 | Direct B2B; partner with HIVE/X8Cloud suppliers |
| Renewable energy equipment | 🟢 High | 2026-2027 | Commercial channels; maquila assembly for Mercosur |
| Agritech / Precision agriculture | 🟢 Medium-High | Near-term | Direct B2B to agro-exporters; Brazil distribution |
| EV & charging infrastructure | 🟡 Medium | 2027+ | Monitor policy; partner with local distributors |
| Telecom RAN/Core equipment | 🔴 Blocked | Requires diplomatic shift | No pathway without recognition change |
| Green hydrogen / Power-to-X | 🟡 Medium | 2027+ | Monitor energy reform; explore non-AI-hub projects |
| Mining equipment & services | 🟡 Medium | 2027-2028 | Monitor subsoil law; partner with international miners |
